chunks: Ali ibn al-Sindi from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who travels to Jeddah for a need, he said: 'He enters (the state of Hajj) without Ihram.'

key_terms.إِحْرَامٍ: Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.الْحَاجَةِ: The need (purpose of travel, distinct from Hajj)
key_terms.جُدَّةَ: Jeddah (a city in Saudi Arabia, gateway to Mecca)

ai.seo_question: Does a traveler to Jeddah need to enter the state of Ihram if they are not performing Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between the ritual state of Ihram and mere entry into the sacred precincts (Haram), ruling that a traveler to Jeddah for general needs does not incur the penalties of breaking Ihram unless they explicitly assume the state. This reflects the Shia juristic view that Ihram is a specific intention-bound status rather than an automatic consequence of geographical proximity to the holy sites, a nuance critical for understanding the *Kaffarah* (expiation) rules detailed in the chapter.
